fields.h1: Build a Wellness Quiz That Names How Each Person Recharges
fields.hero_description: Build a wellness quiz that matches people to a recharge style, suggests one habit to try, and saves answers to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Goes Into a Wellness Quiz Built on Emergent
fields.features_subheading: One prompt gives you the quiz and the table of answers behind it. Ask for a change, and Emergent rebuilds that part.
fields.feature_1:
Questions about ordinary days

Name the styles you want as results, such as Mover or Quiet Recharger. Emergent writes questions about sleep, breaks, and weekends, and maps every option to one style.
fields.feature_2:
Results worded as habits, not scores

Each result says what someone's answers lean toward and offers one small habit to try. Ask for that wording in your prompt, and keep health scores and labels off the screen.
fields.feature_3:
A next step for every style

Point each result to something real: a benefit, a weekend package, a coaching call. Connect your HR or booking tool through its API, and the result screen lists what fits.
fields.feature_4:
An email to whoever follows up

When a client or guest finishes, the coach or guest coordinator gets an email with a link. Answers stay in the app, and employee quizzes saved without names send no alert.
fields.feature_5:
Every answer in a database you own

Each finished quiz is a row in a database you own, with the style, the date, and every answer. Emergent puts no cap on responses, and a company-wide rollout records each one.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and the code on paid plans

Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. Run the quiz on yours. Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans, and change it in your own tools.

fields.usecase_heading: Where a Wellness Quiz Does Its Work
fields.tab_content_1:
Every Connector result opens with the walking group

Quorvale Freight adds the wellness quiz to open enrollment week for its 540 employees. Each style maps to 2 benefits on the result screen. A Connector sees the Thursday lunch walking group and the team volunteer day. Results are saved without names, and HR sees only the count for each style.
fields.tab_content_2:
Duvessa gets the lake weekend that fits a Quiet Recharger

Fenmarsh Retreat puts the quiz on its booking page. Duvessa Pimsley answers 8 questions and lands on Quiet Recharger. Her result page shows the 2-night quiet weekend at the lake house, with May dates open, and a button to request one. Her answers go to the guest table, and the guest coordinator gets an email.
fields.tab_content_3:
Coach Brisbeck reads all 8 of Sabeen's answers first

Before a first call, coach Ama Brisbeck sends every new client the wellness quiz. Sabeen Kreel answers on her phone on Tuesday night and lands on Routine Keeper. Her 8 answers and the result go to her client record, and Ama gets an email. On Wednesday's call, they start with the habit Sabeen picked: a set bedtime.
fields.tab_content_4:
Of 2,180 readers in March, 720 lean toward quiet time

In March, 2,180 readers of The Even Keel finished the quiz linked from the newsletter. Quiet Recharger led with 720 results, ahead of Connector at 610 and Mover at 480, while Routine Keeper drew 370. The editor planned April's 4 issues around rest and quiet time and held a Connector issue for May.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Wellness Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a wellness quiz with results people recognize, a next step for each, and every result tested.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what each result leads to
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with what happens after the result: a benefit to join, a weekend to request, a call with a coach, or one habit to try. That choice shapes every result screen. Put it in your prompt before you write a single question.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick four results a person would be glad to read, such as Mover, Connector, Routine Keeper, and Quiet Recharger. For each, write two sentences on how that person recharges and one habit they could start this week.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask what people do with a free hour, a hard week, or a Saturday morning. Leave out symptoms, weight, medications, and health history. Those belong in a conversation with a professional, and a quiz about habits does its job without them.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write four options per question, one for each style, at about the same length so none looks like the right answer. Check that every style is reachable through at least two questions, and set the order that breaks a tie.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Keep it to one question per screen
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put each question on its own screen with a progress bar, and hold the quiz to 8 questions. Before you share it, take it on a phone and time yourself. If it runs past 2 minutes, cut the weakest question.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Before launch, decide who reads one person's answers and who sees only counts. Save employee results without names. For coaching clients, tell people in one plain line that their coach reads the answers before the first call.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test every result, then share the link
fields.howto_step_7_des: Take the quiz four times, aiming at a different style each time, and confirm the right result screen appears. Open the saved rows and check that each answer landed. Then put the link on your page or in your newsletter.

faq_plan.q: What are some good questions for a wellness quiz?
faq_plan.ref: What are some good questions for a wellness quiz?

prov.original: What are some good questions for a wellness quiz?

faq_plan.a: Good wellness quiz questions ask about ordinary habits: what someone does with a free hour, how they unwind after a hard week, when they go to bed, and who they call when stress builds. Give each question four options of similar length, one per result. Leave symptoms and health history out.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a wellness quiz?
faq_plan.a: Pick your results first, then describe them, the questions, and what each result leads to in a prompt. Emergent's AI survey builder writes the questions and result pages, plus a table that keeps every finished quiz. Take it once for each result before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: How do I write wellness quiz questions and answers that have one right answer?
faq_plan.a: Take each right answer from a published health source and quote it under the question. The CDC, for example, says that most adults need at least 7 hours of sleep each night, which gives a sleep question one sourced answer. Score the total, and show the source beside every miss.

faq_plan.q: When does a wellness quiz work better than a survey?
faq_plan.a: Use a quiz when each person should get something back, such as a style and a habit to try. Use a wellness survey when HR needs to measure how teams feel and compare the numbers year over year. A survey gives the person answering no result of their own.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a wellness quiz have?
faq_plan.a: Eight works well for a quiz with 4 results, and the quiz on this page uses 8. Below 6, a single answer carries too much weight in the result. Above 10, cut any question whose options repeat an earlier one. Emergent puts no cap on how many people take it.

faq_plan.q: How do I follow up after someone takes a wellness quiz?
faq_plan.a: Ask for an email on the result screen, then send the habit for that style a week later with one check-in question: did you try it? Put the reminder in your prompt, and Emergent builds it into the app, which saves each reply beside the original answers.

faq_plan.q: Should a wellness quiz ask for an email before showing the result?
faq_plan.a: No. Show the result first, then ask for an email with a clear reason, such as sending the habit plan for that style. A visitor who has read the result knows what they are signing up for, and the email field can stay optional.

faq_plan.q: Is a wellness quiz the same as a health risk assessment?
faq_plan.a: No. A wellness quiz matches habits and preferences to a result. The CDC describes a health risk assessment as a health questionnaire used to provide individuals with an evaluation of their health risks and quality of life. Keep a quiz to habits, and leave risk questions to an assessment run with health professionals.

faq_plan.q: Can I change wellness quiz questions after the quiz goes live?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Describe the change in a prompt, and Emergent updates the quiz. Ask for a version column as well, so answers saved before the change stay labeled with the questions they answered.

faq_plan.q: Can I offer a wellness quiz in Spanish as well as English?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask for both languages in your prompt, with a language choice on the first screen. Have a native speaker read every result before launch. A habit that reads warmly in English can sound stiff in a word-for-word translation.

quiz.title: Find Your Wellness Style in 8 Everyday Questions
quiz.intro: Eight questions about your ordinary days. Your result names the way your answers lean toward recharging, with one small habit to try this week.

questions.text: After a long week, what helps you feel like yourself again?

options.text: A walk, a swim, or a bike ride
Dinner or a call with people you like
Getting the house and the week ahead in order
A quiet evening with a book or a bath

questions.text: You have a free hour on a weekday. How do you spend it?

options.text: Out the door for some kind of movement
Catching up with a friend or a neighbor
Prepping meals or planning tomorrow
Sitting somewhere quiet with no screen

questions.text: Which small habit would you most like to keep?

options.text: Taking the stairs and a lunchtime walk
Checking in with one person each day
Going to bed and waking at the same time
10 minutes of quiet before the day starts

questions.text: When stress builds up, what do you reach for first?

options.text: Something physical to burn it off
Someone to talk it through with
A list, so the next step is clear
Time alone to slow everything down

questions.text: Pick the weekend plan that sounds best.

options.text: A hike or a game of pickup basketball
A cookout with friends and family
A slow morning, errands done, a tidy home
A long nap and an afternoon in the garden

questions.text: What makes a workday feel balanced?

options.text: Getting up from the desk every hour
A good conversation with a coworker
Finishing on time with tomorrow planned
A real lunch break away from messages

questions.text: Which wellness program would you sign up for?

options.text: A step challenge with a weekly goal
A team volunteer day
A sleep and morning routine series
A guided breathing or quiet-time session

questions.text: What would you tell a friend who feels run down?

options.text: Get outside and move for a bit
Call someone and make plans
Pick one routine and stick with it for a week
Take an evening off and rest

results.title: Mover
results.description: Your answers lean toward recharging through movement: walks, rides, games, anything that gets you out of a chair. Try putting one short walk on the calendar each day, at the same time, and treat it like a meeting.

results.title: Connector
results.description: Your answers lean toward recharging with other people. A good talk or a shared meal resets your week. Try one standing plan each week, such as a Thursday walk or a Sunday call, so time with people does not depend on luck.

results.title: Routine Keeper
results.description: Your answers lean toward recharging through order: a plan for tomorrow, regular hours, a tidy space. Pick one routine to protect this week, such as a set bedtime or a Sunday plan for the week, and keep it for 7 days.

results.title: Quiet Recharger
results.description: Your answers lean toward recharging in quiet: time alone, no screens, a slower pace. Try blocking 20 minutes each day with no messages and nothing to finish, and guard it the way you would guard a meeting.
